What the estimate includes

The estimate adds GGUF file bytes, estimated KV cache and the runtime allowance you enter. The available budget is unified memory minus the amount you reserve for macOS and other apps. File listings often use decimal GB. The results use GiB, with 1 GiB equal to 1,073,741,824 bytes.

FP16 KV bytes = context × layers × KV heads × head dimension × 2 × 2

One factor of 2 counts keys and values. The other is the byte size of FP16. This is raw cache for one sequence and full attention. A custom model must have uniform attention layers and the same width for each key and value head. Use the exact architecture and combined size of all GGUF shards.

Runtime allocation also depends on buffer sizes, alignment, parallel sequences, offloading and cache format. Sliding-window, hybrid and latent-attention architectures use different cache layouts. A positive budget is a starting point for a load test. It provides no performance or model compatibility guarantee.

For example, the Qwen2.5 7B Q4_K_M preset has 4.36 GiB of files. Its raw FP16 cache estimates are 0.44 GiB at 8,192 tokens and 1.75 GiB at 32,768. With a 1 GiB runtime allowance, the same model estimates 5.80 and 7.11 GiB respectively.

Compare with a measured Ollama run

In an earlier Ollama 0.40.18 test on an 18 GiB M3 Pro, we loaded Qwen2.5 0.5B Q4_K_M at two context lengths. The same 491,400,032-byte GGUF was used both times. The cache column applies the formula above. Ollama’s /api/ps reported the other column.

Same model, two context settings
ContextRaw FP16 cacheReported load
2,04824 MiB297.27 MiB
8,19296 MiB418.79 MiB

The raw cache estimate grew by 72 MiB. Ollama’s reported load grew by about 122 MiB. The values use different accounting, and the test did not isolate every allocation. Read the original API snapshots.

Verify on your Mac

  1. Load the exact local tag with the context you plan to use. For a repeatable check, set the request context and confirm the running value.
  2. While the model is loaded, run ollama ps. Check the processor split and the model row. The native /api/ps also exposes byte counts. Read the GPU and CPU comparison.
  3. In Activity Monitor’s Memory tab, check memory pressure and swap used while sending a representative request. If pressure or swap climbs, test a shorter context or a smaller quantized model first.

Model data and sources

Presets use Qwen’s source architecture settings and the combined bytes of the official Q4_K_M files.
